articles.title: Effect of blood transfusion on respiratory failure in severe trauma patients: A post hoc analysis of a randomized multicenter trial in Japan.
articles.abstract: Severe trauma patients often need a large amount of blood transfusion including red blood cells (RBCs), fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and platelet. The blood transfusion can cause serious transfusion-related adverse events including respiratory complications, however, the risks of blood transfusion in trauma patients have not been well documented. We evaluated the hypothesis that the amount of blood transfusion during the acute post-injury phase was associated with respiratory failure among severe trauma patients at risk of active bleeding using a database of a randomized multicenter trial. We used data from the Restrictive Transfusion Strategy for Critically Injured Patients (RESTRIC) trial, a cluster-randomized, crossover, non-inferiority multicenter trial conducted in Japan from May 7, 2019 to October 31, 2021 in Japan. The trial enrolled adult trauma patients transferred to the emergency department with severe bleeding or suspected severe bleeding and circulatory shock. All patients registered in this trial were included in this study. The primary outcome measure was the occurrence of respiratory failure within 7 days after admission. A logistic regression analysis on respiratory failure adjusted for sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), chest Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) score, and the amount of RBCs, FFP, and platelet transfusions within 24 h was performed. Of 417 trauma patients, 40 (9.8%) developed respiratory failure. Logistic regression analysis revealed that sex, chest AIS score, and platelet transfusion volume were associated with respiratory failure with 7 days after admission after adjustment (odds ratio [OR]: 0.300, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.113-0.794, p = 0.015, OR: 1.732, 95% CI: 1.267-2.367, p < 0.001, OR: 1.071, 95% CI: 1.021-1.122, p = 0.005 respectively). ISS, RBC, and FFP transfusions were not associated with respiratory failure (all p ≥ 0.05). Among severe trauma patients with severe bleeding or circulatory shock transferred to the emergency department, platelet transfusion volume within 24 h may be a risk factor for respiratory failure within 7 days after admission. In contrast, RBC and FFP transfusions were not associated with respiratory failure.

articles.title: Bacterial cellulose-sericin gold nanoparticle conduit functionalized with GDNF for peripheral nerve regeneration: An experimental sciatic nerve injury model in rats.
articles.abstract: Although the application of autografts continues to be regarded as the gold standard for the treatment of peripheral nerve injuries, there exists a necessity for alternative grafting materials. This study investigates the effects of a nerve conduit obtained from bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes modified with gold nanoparticles (AuNP) and functionalized with the GDNF neurotrophic factor on repair in peripheral nerve injury. Bacterial cellulose membranes obtained from Gluconacetobacter xylinus cell culture were modified with sericin-gold nanoparticles produced by green synthesis and functionalized with glial-derived neurotrophic factor to become conduits. A unilateral 8 mm sciatic nerve defect was created in Wistar rats (n = 21). Rats were divided into three groups as autograft (n = 7), BC-AuNP (n = 7), and BC-AuNP/GDNF (n = 7). Gait analysis and electromyography (EMG) measurements were performed at the end of the 8th week. Tissues from the sciatic nerve were obtained for histological and immunohistochemical analysis. By the result of the 8th week, the BC-AuNPs/GDNF group attained results comparable to those of the autograft group, as indicated by the sciatic function index derived from gait analysis and EMG measurements. Examinations of axon diameters, myelin sheath thickness, and vessel count demonstrated that the autograft and BC-AuNPs/GDNF groups exhibited significantly elevated values in comparison to the BC-AuNPs group. In the management of peripheral nerve injury, the application of BC-AuNP/GDNF yielded healing outcomes that were comparable to those achieved through autograft, both functionally and histologically.

articles.title: Profound motorcycle risks: a national mileage exposure-adjusted analysis.
articles.abstract: Motorcycle crashes (MCC) account for a minority of vehicle miles in the United States, but their exposure-adjusted burden among trauma admissions is not well defined. The purpose of this study was to compare the injury burden of MCC versus motor vehicle crashes (MVC) using outcomes standardized by annual vehicle miles traveled (VMT). A retrospective cohort study of American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs (ACS-TQP) admissions from 2017 to 2023 was performed for adults aged 18-80 years admitted after MCC or MVC. Primary outcomes were admission, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality per 100 million VMT using Federal Highway Administration denominators. Motorcycle VMT was used for MCC, and light-duty vehicle VMT was used for MVC. Secondary outcomes included Injury Severity Score thresholds (≥16 and ≥25), severe head/neck injury, open long-bone fracture, ventilation, and return to the operating room. Relative risks (RRs) were estimated using binomial regression models with a log link. Among 1,419,094 admissions, 334,310 followed MCC and 1,084,784 followed MVC. MCC accounted for 23.6% of admissions but only 0.71% of included VMT. Per 100 million VMT, MCC had higher rates of admission (236.4 vs. 5.49; rate ratio, 43.0), ICU admission (70.8 vs. 1.57; rate ratio, 45.1), amputation (5.06 vs. 0.028; rate ratio, 183.0), and in-hospital mortality (6.4 vs. 0.12; rate ratio, 51.6). Among admitted patients, MCC was associated with higher risks of open long-bone fracture (14.7% vs. 6.6%; RR, 2.22), amputation (2.1% vs. 0.5%; RR, 4.25), and in-hospital mortality (2.7% vs. 2.2%; RR, 1.20). MCCs contribute a disproportionately high burden of severe trauma in the United States, with higher mileage-adjusted rates of ICU admission, amputation, and in-hospital mortality than MVCs.

articles.title: Indicators of Surfers as Aquatic Rescuers in Coastal Environments in Brazil: Profile and Potential Based on Cluster Analysis.
articles.abstract: IntroductionDrowning is a major public health problem and ranks among the leading causes of death worldwide, especially in low- and middle-income countries. Surfers may play a relevant role as informal aquatic rescuers.ObjectiveTo assess the potential of surfers to act as aquatic rescuers by analyzing their knowledge of rescue and first aid in Brazilian coastal environments.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 171 surfers over 18 years of age, of both sexes, recruited by convenience through an electronic questionnaire. Participants who self-reported autonomy to paddle beyond the breaking zone and catch waves without assistance were included. The instrument comprised sociodemographic data, surfing experience, risk perception, knowledge of sea conditions, first-aid training, and history of rescues. Cluster analysis using the K-means algorithm was employed to group participants based on variables related to experience, risk perception, and technical knowledge, identifying homogeneous profiles regarding their potential for rescue activities.ResultsTwo distinct clusters were identified. Cluster 1 showed lower experience, less formal qualification, and less previous involvement in rescues. Cluster 2 comprised older surfers (43 ± 9 years), with longer surfing experience, predominantly male (79%), advanced technical level, professional involvement with surfing, first-aid training, and a higher frequency of rescues performed (p < 0.05).ConclusionSurfers with greater experience, higher technical level, and first-aid training show greater potential to act as informal aquatic rescuers. A substantial proportion of participants lack formal training, underscoring the need for structured training strategies.

articles.title: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) as a prognostic marker in polytrauma: predicting 30-day mortality and coagulation support needs.
articles.abstract: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS), derived from a simple formula based on haematocrit and haemoglobin values, has been associated with an unfavourable prognosis in many cardiovascular conditions, demonstrating a correlation with volume overload and the haemodynamic status of the patient. Indeed, ePVS was demonstrated to estimate the degree of congestion and was independently associated with cardiovascular outcomes, rehospitalization, and death in patients with heart failure (HF), confirming its prognostic value also in inflammatory pathologies. Due to its easy and immediate availability even in the emergency department (ED), ePVS may be useful in trauma patients to improve their initial evaluation and management. The aim of this retrospective observational study was to evaluate the role of ePVS at ED admission in predicting mortality and blood products use, red blood cells (RBC) and fresh frozen plasma (FFP), in trauma. We included 790 patients, of whom 67.7% were male; mean age 43.9 years; median Injury Severity Score (ISS) 7.5. The 30-day mortality rate was 2.8% (22/790). The median ePVS was significantly increased in deceased as compared to survivors (5.76; 4.79-8.36 versus 4.41; 3.92-5.05; p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS is an independent risk factor even after adjusting for other variables associated with 30-day mortality (odds radio, OR of 1.23; 95% confidence interval, CI 1.016-1.478, p = 0.034). Prediction of 30-day mortality for ePVS showed an AUROC of 0.776 (95% CI 0.666-0.887). Moreover, ePVS showed a positive correlation with the number of packed RBC and FFP units transfused, both during ED management, within the first 24 h, and over the entire hospital stay. The present findings suggest ePVS as a quick and easy tool to predict 30-day mortality and the need for blood resuscitation in trauma patients. Future studies may validate ePVS as a quick and easy tool for trauma victims' stratification and for predicting resource needs and mortality.

articles.title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain. Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality. The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p < 0.001). Death due to haemorrhagic shock was significantly more frequent in the "Super Early" group (36.8%) compared to the "Early" group (13.7%) (p < 0.001). A regression model was adjusted to determine the independent predictors of mortality. Time to emergency laparotomy was not an independent predictor of mortality. However, increased ISS (OR = 1.04, p = 0.049), age (OR = 1.03, p = 0.037) and decreased systolic blood pressure (OR = 0.98, p = 0.025) were found to be significant predictors of mortality. The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

articles.title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma. A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge." Eight patients were admitted within a 10-day window following high-energy injuries from the challenge. The cohort showed a female predominance (62.5%) with a mean age of 13.25 (±1.03) years. The high-velocity mechanism led to atypical, severe injury patterns distinct from routine accidental falls. We observed an unusual cluster of severe distal forearm fractures in five patients, which uniformly required surgical treatment. Three patients even suffered bilateral distal radius fractures. Additional associated injuries included fractures of the ulnar styloid process (n = 5) and concomitant TFCC tears (n = 2), reflecting the high-energy nature of the challenge. The rapid, viral spread of physical social media challenges such as the 'Superman Challenge' can lead to dangerous injury mechanisms involving high-velocity trauma among children and adolescents. These trends could lead to sudden, localized clusters of atypical high-energy injuries-a scenario that, under specific conditions, risks overtaxing conventional healthcare systems, as previously demonstrated in the literature. Medical staff need to be aware of changing digital behaviors, which represent a new mechanism of injury in pediatric trauma.

articles.title: When Less Is More: Noninvasive Rewarming of a Severely Hypothermic Trauma Patient.
Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models. Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001). Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay. Not applicable.

articles.title: A Drone-Integrated Artificial Intelligence-Based System for Mass-Casualty Triage and Remote Monitoring.
articles.abstract: Triage and data transfer are critical to the medical management of mass-casualty incidents (MCIs). However, the chaotic nature of such events makes it difficult to classify casualties according to structured triage protocols. Furthermore, even when triage is implemented effectively, communication disruptions between the incident scene and dispatch centers can hinder response operations. The aim of this study was to present a drone-integrated system that enables non-contact vital sign measurement, remote triage, and real-time data transmission during MCIs. The system development process involved three steps: (1) developing the Vital-Sign Measurement Module; (2) developing the Triage Decision Support Module; and (3) developing the User Interfaces and Data Transmission Module to enable information transmission between dispatch centers and response teams. Within the Vital-Sign Measurement Module, heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), oxygen saturation (SpO2), and body temperature (BT) measurement algorithms were developed using the following techniques, respectively: video-based photoplethysmography (vPPG), analysis of thermal temperature fluctuations around the nose, a regression-based neural network approach, and heat maps and thermal thresholding. A pilot study was conducted under controlled indoor conditions to evaluate the accuracy of these algorithms. The system can measure vital signs by processing drone-captured images, can provide triage decision support, and can transmit victims' locations, vital signs, and triage categories to response teams and dispatch centers via dedicated user interfaces. A pilot evaluation of the Vital-Sign Measurement Module showed that the relative accuracy rate of the non-contact vital-sign measurement algorithms ranged from 86% to 99%. The system provides an innovative approach to improving medical response management in MCIs by enabling remote triage and monitoring. Its non-contact vital sign measurement, triage decision support, and near real-time data transmission capabilities provide an infrastructure that can contribute to faster response and improved operational coordination. However, further field trials and development are required to improve the robustness of the vital-sign measurement algorithms to motion, to improve their adaptability to changing environmental conditions, and to maintain high accuracy despite individual differences.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity point-of-care troponin assays in emergency department for patients presenting with chest pain: a systematic review.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices (turnaround time <20 min) may significantly reduce time to diagnosis. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November, 2025. Studies were included if they investigated patients greater than or equal to 18 years presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy [sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value] for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Studies were assessed for risk of bias and applicability using the QUADAS-3 tool. We identified 436 articles. The 11 included studies consisted of both derivation and validation studies, including a total of 10 115 patients. The hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single-test rule-out upon arrival at the ED, showing the following sensitivity and NPV: Atellica VTLi sensitivity 98.8-100% for troponin less than 4 ng/L (NPV: 99.8-100%) and 100% for troponin less than 7 ng/L (NPV 100%). Pathfast sensitivity 96.3-100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV: 98.1-100%). i-STAT sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin less than 5 ng/L (NPV: 100%). TriageTrue sensitivity of 100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV 100%). VTLi, Pathfast, and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99th percentile with a 0 + 1/2/3 h troponin protocol. Reported sensitivities: VTLi 64.8-100%, Pathfast 87% for plasma and 83% for whole blood, and TriageTrue 79.8%. Hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration into the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule-out of AMI in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.

articles.title: Human Factors-Driven Optimization of Pediatric Resuscitation Workflow Using Integrated Color-Coded Systems: A Randomized Crossover Study.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated whether a human factors-driven, integrated, color-coded resuscitation system that combines equipment standardization and prefilled-medication cognitive aids improves workflow efficiency and accuracy compared with a conventional crash cart during simulated pediatric resuscitations. A prospective, randomized, crossover simulation study was conducted with 28 health care professionals. Each team participated in 2 pediatric resuscitation scenarios using either the SCC or the CCCC in random order. All sessions were video-recorded to measure equipment retrieval and medication preparation times. Statistical comparisons were made using paired statistical tests appropriate for crossover designs, with significance set at P<0.05. Use of the CCCC significantly reduced the time to locate airway devices (13.1±6.9 vs. 41.7±22 s, P<0.001) and airway adjuncts (13.8±11.9 vs. 30.8±17.4 s, P=0.03). Prefilled color-coded syringes significantly reduced medication preparation time (median: 16 vs. 19 s; absolute reduction 3 s, P=0.04), with no dosing errors observed. Teams using the CCCC demonstrated more consistent workflow and fewer procedural delays. In this randomized crossover simulation study, the integrated color-coded system reduced equipment retrieval and medication preparation times for selected pediatric resuscitation tasks. These findings are limited to the simulation setting and should be interpreted in light of the Broselow framework's use for both cart organization and assessment of correct equipment selection. Further research is needed to evaluate the feasibility of color-coded prefilled syringes and determine whether the observed workflow benefits translate to real-world pediatric patient care.

articles.title: Association Between Childhood Opportunity Index and Pediatric Emergency Department Utilization of Youth With Experiences of Trafficking: A National Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: To understand associations between the Child Opportunity Index (COI), a neighborhood-based measure of resources that influence child health and development, and pediatric ED utilization among youth with experiences of trafficking in the United States, as well as to describe their range of COI, sociodemographic characteristics, and pediatric ED utilization. This was a retrospective, observational, cohort study. We identified (by ICD-10 code) youth with experiences of trafficking who presented to pediatric EDs across 50 US children's hospitals between January 2018 and February 2023 within the Pediatric Health Information System database. Descriptive analyses and multivariate regression were performed. We identified 908 youth with experiences of trafficking who presented to pediatric EDs. Among them, 55% (n=499) were from neighborhoods with Very Low and Low COI, while 45% (n=409) were from neighborhoods with Moderate to Very High COI. Mental health diagnoses were common (n=584, 65.3%), and mental health, child abuse, and physical trauma were the top diagnosis categories for ED visits. Low-resource intensity visits were uncommon (12.8%). One-third of patients had an ED visit in the year prior. We did not find major statistically significant associations between COI and hospital utilization. In this cohort of youth with experiences of trafficking, all levels of COI and a wide range of visit acuity levels were represented. Further study is needed to better understand the prevalence and health needs of youth with experiences of trafficking who receive ED care, to develop effective screening and intervention programs to support these youth.

articles.title: Continuous Pulse Oximetry Analysis to Predict Outcomes in Young Infants With Bronchiolitis Presenting to the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Predictive analytics using continuously measured vital signs from bedside monitors has improved outcomes in critically ill children. We investigated whether continuous pulse oximetry data collected during emergency department (ED) evaluation can identify infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis at low risk of respiratory deterioration. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis who presented to a tertiary-care pediatric ED from November 2021 to November 2025. Infants were identified using the ICD-10 code with manual eligibility confirmation. Heart rate and oxygen saturation features were generated from continuous pulse oximetry during the first 2 hours of ED evaluation. The primary outcome was respiratory deterioration within 24 hours of ED arrival, defined as initiation of high-flow nasal cannula, continuous/bilevel positive airway pressure, or invasive mechanical ventilation. Data were split into derivation and validation cohorts (70/30, stratified by outcome). An L2-regularized logistic regression model estimated the probability of respiratory deterioration, with a classification threshold selected to prioritize sensitivity. Of 290 infants meeting clinical eligibility, 117 had sufficient continuous pulse oximetry data; 57 (49%) had respiratory deterioration. The primary model included 3 features: the median and interquartile range (IQR) of heart rate, and oxygen saturation IQR. In the validation cohort, the model showed moderate sensitivity (0.78, 95% CI: 0.58-0.95) and fair discrimination (AUROC=0.78, 95% CI: 0.62-0.93). We derived and validated a model using data from continuous pulse oximetry to identify low-risk infants with bronchiolitis. With further refinement and integration into monitor design systems, this approach may enhance clinical utility of continuous pulse oximetry.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Low-Acuity EMS Transport to the Emergency Department: An Observational Study Guided by the Andersen Behavioral Model.
articles.abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) demand is increasing, with a growing proportion of low-acuity encounters. Prior studies are limited by regional sampling, inconsistent definitions, narrow observation periods, and limited theoretical grounding. The objective of this study was to identify predisposing, enabling, and need-based factors associated with EMS transport among low-acuity emergency department (ED) patients, guided by Andersen's Behavioral Model of Health Services Use. We conducted a secondary, retrospective observational study using a 10% random sample of multicenter electronic health record data from 21 EDs in the southeastern United States. Eligible visits included: (1) patient age >17 years, (2) occurred between January 1, 2016, and April 29, 2025, (3) triaged as Emergency Severity Index 4 or 5, and (4) ended in a final visit disposition of discharge. The primary outcome was arrival at the ED by EMS. We categorized independent variables as predisposing, enabling, or need-based factors according to Andersen's model. We used multivariable logistic regression to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 41,761 low-acuity ED encounters, 3,232 (7.7%) arrived by EMS. Higher odds of EMS use were observed for older age (per 10-year increase; aOR 1.33, 95% CI = 1.30-1.36), male sex (aOR 1.20, 95% CI = 1.12-1.30), being retired or disabled (aOR 3.60, 95% CI = 3.15-4.10), being unemployed (aOR 2.26, 95% CI = 2.04-2.52), having a nighttime presentation (aOR 1.63, 95% CI = 1.51-1.76), and mental health diagnosis (aOR 1.76, 95% CI = 1.62-1.90). Lower odds of EMS arrival were observed for white race (aOR 0.89, 95% CI = 0.83-0.96), established primary care (aOR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.53-0.62), weekend presentation (aOR 0.91; 95% CI = 0.84-0.99), and visits during (aOR 0.63, 95% CI = 0.55-0.71) or after (aOR 0.54, 95% CI = 0.48-0.61) the COVID-19 period. Rurality, insurance, and primary language were not associated with EMS use. Among low-acuity ED patients, EMS arrival was associated with older age, unemployment or disability, no established primary care clinician, and a previous mental health diagnosis. These characteristics identify a population that may be served by alternatives to ambulance transport, such as treat-in-place and alternative destination pathways, when paired with expanded access to primary care and behavioral health resources.

articles.title: Missed Opportunities for Prehospital Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma.
articles.abstract: Prehospital blood transfusion has been associated with improved outcomes among pediatric trauma patients, but its utilization nationally remains poorly understood. We recently conducted a similar study that builds upon the findings of the investigation by Ramgopal et al. to identify potential missed opportunities for prehospital transfusion in pediatric trauma. We utilized the National EMS Information System dataset from 2018-2023 to identify emergency medical services (EMS) responses for pediatric (<18 years of age) trauma patients. We identified trauma patients using the CDC Injury Mortality Diagnosis Matrix related ICD-10 codes. We identified patients at increased risk of benefiting from a transfusion using age-adjusted positive shock index thresholds. The outcome of interested was prehospital blood or blood product transfusion. We found there were 1,663,601 total 9-1-1 EMS activations to a scene for pediatric trauma. There were 363,844 patients with a positive shock index who were considered to be at increased risk of benefiting from a prehospital transfusion, but only 287 (0.1%) of these patients received a prehospital transfusion. Only 10 (2%) of the 468 patients who experienced a cardiac arrest after the arrival of EMS to the scene received a hospital transfusion. Together, our results indicate prehospital transfusion rates ranging from 0.1% to 1.01% among potentially eligible pediatric trauma patients. Although positive shock index does not confirm hemorrhagic shock, these findings suggest underutilization of prehospital blood transfusion among pediatric trauma patients.

articles.title: Personalized Remote Patient Management in Heart Failure : From Implanted Hemodynamic Monitoring Toward an Artificial Intelligence-Supported Adaptive Care Cycle.
articles.abstract: Implanted pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) monitoring provides an early window on imminent worsening heart failure (HF). Randomized trials demonstrated that PAP-guided management significantly reduces HF hospitalizations, but substantial residual risk persists despite recent major advances in HF pharmacotherapy. We review lessons from PAP-guided remote patient management and examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could support more individualized eligibility assessment and multimodal longitudinal surveillance within a patient-centered adaptive care cycle to further improve clinical outcomes. HF is increasingly recognized as a systemic disease characterized, across HF phenotypes, by multiple cardiac and non-cardiac comorbidities. CHAMPION, GUIDE-HF, and MONITOR-HF did not systematically incorporate comorbidity-related risk into patient selection, while PAP-guided treatment focused predominantly on diuretic adjustment, and monitoring strategies were not adapted to individual disease trajectories. AI could help integrate multidimensional phenotyping to estimate individual risk and expected benefit pre-implant, use comprehensive longitudinal monitoring data to support personalized, actionable clinical decision-making, and enable dynamic adaptation of monitoring intensity tailored to the disease trajectory. This may improve clinical outcomes, reduce healthcare professional workload, enhance patient experience and treatment adherence, and increase cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Harnessing the potential of response surface methodology-based optimized scaffolds in volumetric muscle loss repair in sprague dawley rat.
articles.abstract: Volumetric Muscle Loss (VML) is a complex tissue injury characterised by loss of tissue beyond the body's intrinsic regenerative capacity, resulting in impaired muscle regeneration and functional recovery. Limited cellular proliferation and poor in situ healing make VML one of the most challenging issues in tissue engineering. Conventional approaches of acidic gelling and use of artificial substrates compromise the structural integrity, biocompatibility and functional performance of tissue-engineered constructs. Moreover, the irregular geometries of muscle defects make surgical reconstruction technically challenging and often insufficient to achieve complete functional restoration. In this study, a novel porous scaffold containing collagen, fibronectin, and raloxifene (a cell-proliferative drug) was prepared for VML repair. The concentration of scaffold components was optimized using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to obtain an effective scaffold composition. The regenerative efficacy of the optimized scaffold was evaluated in a Sprague-Dawley rat model of VML. The results suggested that RSM-optimized scaffold significantly improved VML repair after 21 days (p < 0.05) in vivo. A prominent development of muscle fibre and deposition of collagen was observed. At molecular level, a significant increase in the expression of MyoD and STAT3 genes was observed in optimized scaffold group, suggesting enhanced myogenesis and tissue repair. The findings indicate that RSM may be utilized to optimize the tissue-engineered construct to improve VML repair.

articles.title: Acellular fish-skin grafting complex soft tissue defects in orthopedic trauma: Technique and outcomes of a consecutive case series.
articles.abstract: This article describes a surgical technique for applying an acellular fish-skin graft (Kerecis Omega3 Wound; Kerecis, Ísafjörður, Iceland) in orthopedic trauma and reports outcomes from a consecutive series of patients treated at an urban Level I trauma center. After institutional review board approval, we reviewed 27 adult patients with complex extremity wounds who were treated with acellular fish-skin grafting between January 1st, 2023, and December 30th, 2025. Wound etiologies included traumatic soft tissue injuries, postoperative wound dehiscence, necrotizing soft tissue infections, and chronic osteomyelitis with associated soft tissue compromise. Acellular fish-skin grafting was indicated in this series of patients for full-thickness skin loss (or deeper), including those with exposed tendons, bone, or ligaments, in whom flap reconstruction was contraindicated. Patients underwent serial irrigation and debridement followed by application of an acellular fish-skin graft. The primary outcome was complete wound healing without flap-based soft-tissue reconstruction. Secondary outcomes included the number of graft applications, duration of negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT), time to split-thickness skin grafting (STSG), and all complications. Acellular fish-skin grafting facilitated wound healing in most patients, including those with infection, exposed bone, tendon, and/or ligaments, and substantial medical and social comorbidities. Twenty-two patients (84%) achieved definitive wound coverage without flap reconstruction. Five patients (19%) were referred to plastic surgery after grafting. Two ultimately achieved limb salvage with local wound care alone, whereas the remaining three required amputation. None of the referred patients were salvaged with flap reconstruction. One patient died on postoperative day two from unrelated medical causes, and one was lost to follow-up. Consequently, acellular fish-skin grafting may be a useful adjunct in managing complex orthopedic trauma wounds, particularly in high-risk patients or in settings with limited access to reconstructive surgery. Prospective comparative studies are needed to better define indications, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Comparative study of autologous bone graft and bone morphogenetic protein-2 for bone regeneration using a novel rabbit Masquelet technique model.
articles.abstract: The Masquelet technique is widely used for reconstructing critical-sized bone defects; however, autologous bone grafting (ABG) is associated with donor-site morbidity such as pain and bleeding. Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) has attracted attention as a potential alternative strategy for promoting bone regeneration. Studies on direct comparisons between BMP-2 and autologous bone grafting within the context of the Masquelet technique are limited. The purpose of this study was to establish a novel rabbit femoral Masquelet model and compare the bone regenerative capacity of ABG with β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) loaded with BMP-2. A 20-mm segmental defect was created in the femur of 24-week-old New Zealand White rabbits and stabilized with a locking plate. The defect was filled with polymethyl methacrylate cement, which was removed four weeks later to induce membrane formation. The defect was subsequently filled with autologous iliac bone (ABG group) or β-TCP granules containing BMP-2 (BMP-2 group). Bone regeneration was evaluated 12 weeks after the second surgery using radiographic, histological, micro-computed tomography (μCT), and biomechanical analyses. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated satisfactory bone union in both groups, without substantial difference in union rate. Histological analysis showed cortical continuity and new bone formation in both groups. μ-CT revealed that the bone volume/tissue volume ratio of total calcified callus was significantly higher in the ABG group, whereas the tissue mineral density was significantly higher in the BMP-2 group. Biomechanical testing showed no significant differences in ultimate stress, extrinsic stiffness, or failure energy between the two groups. In this rabbit femoral Masquelet model, BMP-2 delivered with β-TCP achieved bone regeneration comparable to that of autologous bone grafting. These findings suggest that BMP-2 may represent a promising option for bone reconstruction using the Masquelet technique.

articles.title: Leveraging Military-Civilian Partnerships in Crisis: A Case Study of the Las Vegas Response to COVID-19.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in civilian healthcare surge capacity, highlighting the potential for military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) to augment public health emergency responses. The Las Vegas Military-Civilian Partnership (LV MCP), a unique collaboration, offers a case study of such integration. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of the LV MCP, specifically the workload of US Air Force (USAF) pulmonary and critical care medicine (PCCM) physicians, on the Las Vegas civilian healthcare system during the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective review analyzed USAF PCCM physician workload data at University Medical Center (UMC) of Southern Nevada from 2019 to 2023. Data included critical care encounters (CPT codes 99291 and 99292) and COVID-19 encounters (ICD-10 coding). Staffing of 5 USAF PCCM physicians was maintained, with 7 individuals rotating. We assessed changes in the volume of critical care and COVID-19-specific encounters managed by USAF PCCM physicians at UMC. Analysis indicated USAF PCCM physicians reported 19,155 encounters between 2019 and 2023. Encounters peaked at 4,648 in 2020, then declined to 3,155 by 2023. From 2019 to 2020, critical care encounters increased by 1,180, from 1,010 to 2,190. In 2020, 846 (38.6%) of the 2,190 critical care encounters were COVID-19-related. The highest workload occurred during 2020 and 2021, aligning with COVID-19 surges. Of the 2,914 COVID-19-related encounters, 1,892 (64.9%) were classified as critical care-reflecting strong response capability and return to baseline operations. The LV MCP is an effective model for military medical support during a protracted public health crisis. Its preexisting, integrated structure enabled a rapid and sustained surge response, significantly increasing critical care capacity in a medically underserved region without requiring ad hoc federal deployments or DSCA. This underscores the value of embedded military-civilian partnerships as a resilient, efficient strategy for future emergency preparedness, advocating comprehensive data collection to inform integrated responses.

articles.title: Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.
articles.abstract: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories. A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment and mortality. Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

Anaesthesiologists Under Strain: Burnout and Its Associated Factors in a Conflict-affected Context, a Cross-sectional Study.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Anaesthesiologists are particularly vulnerable to burnout due to extended working hours, high-pressure situations, limited patient interactions, multiple responsibilities, and inherent tensions in relationships with surgeons and administrators. The study aimed to explore burnout levels and the factors associated with them among anaesthesiologists in a conflict-affected setting. A cross-sectional study was carried out between May 2024 and August 2025 using a voluntary, anonymous, and electronic survey. The Copenhagen Burnout Inventory, demographics, and practice environment questions were included. Statistical analyses were conducted to identify factors associated with personal, work-related, and client-related burnout. A significance threshold of 0.05 was applied. Among the 82 anaesthesiologists, 57% experienced personal burnout, 51% experienced work-related burnout, and 28% experienced client-related burnout. Positive and significant associations were observed between working longer hours and personal burnout (adjusted ß [95% confidence interval (CI)]=15.6 (0.88; 30.3); P=0.04) and work-related burnout [adjusted ß (95% CI)=17.7 (3.68; 31.7); P=0.01], as well as between covering five or more night shifts per month and client-related burnout [adjusted ß (95% CI)=15.3 (3.86; 26.7); P=0.009]. The findings reveal concerning levels of burnout among anaesthesiologists in conflict-affected regions, which is particularly important given the ongoing regional conflict and limited conflict-specific data, and highlight the potential role of modifiable predictors and associated factors. Targeted interventions are essential to support anaesthesiologists' well-being and ensure the effective functioning of healthcare institutions in such settings. Future studies with larger, randomly selected samples are warranted to further explore this issue.

Impact of Structured Preoperative Counseling on Anaesthesia Preference in Elective Cesarean Delivery: A Prospective Study.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: To assess changes in anaesthesia preference before and after structured preoperative counseling and to identify factors associated with anaesthesia preference among women scheduled for elective cesarean delivery. This prospective, single-center, single-arm, pre-post observational study included 200 pregnant women classified as the American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing demographic characteristics, obstetric history, previous anaesthesia experience, level of knowledge, and anaesthesia preference, both before and after counseling. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 22.0, and a P value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. At baseline, 53% of patients preferred spinal anaesthesia and 47% preferred general anaesthesia. Following counseling, the preference for spinal anaesthesia increased to 88.5% (P < 0.001). Increasing age was associated with a decreased likelihood of choosing spinal anaesthesia [odds ratio (OR)=0.94, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.89-0.99], whereas higher education (OR=1.78, 95% CI: 1.05-3.02), prior knowledge (OR=1.65, 95% CI: 1.02-2.68), and previous spinal anaesthesia experience (OR=2.95, 95% CI: 1.65-5.28) were identified as independent predictors of spinal anaesthesia preference. No significant association was found between smoking and anaesthesia preference, or between comorbidities and anaesthesia preference. The postoperative satisfaction rate with the anaesthesia was 91.5%. Following structured preoperative counseling, the preference for neuraxial anaesthesia increased among women scheduled for elective cesarean delivery. These findings suggest that standardized patient education may be a useful component of preoperative anaesthesia assessment.
